title: Short-cycle budget realignment & headcount trigger matrix (operational worksheet)
body:
Purpose:
This is a short-cycle operational worksheet for reflowing FY26 Q3 budgets across product, SRE, and customer success in response to recent token-price pressure. The goal is to define deterministic hiring and spend gates that finance, product leads, and hiring managers can apply week-to-week while we run the pricing experiment and measure take-rate impacts.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Finance (ops), Product PMs (hosted/dedicated), Talent/People Ops, Solutions Eng.
- Scope: 12-week planning window (rolling), covers non-capex spend reallocation, provisional hiring pauses, and micro-budget transfers between feature buckets.

Context and key assumptions (explicit):
1) Revenue / take-rate shock: a 10–25% reduction in paid usage velocity observed in last 4 weeks in small-mid customers. We model conservative (-10%), baseline (-18%), and tail (-25%).
2) Token unit economics: blended marginal cost per 1k tokens = $0.86 (current model mix); managed reduction via quantization & routing allows a near-term 12% cost save cap.
3) Hiring lead time: backend infra hires 8–10 weeks from req to start; product hires 6–8 weeks; junior SRE ramp 4–6 weeks to meaningful throughput.
4) Buffer target: maintain 6-week payroll runway for contractors used for burst capacity.

High-level decision rule (single-sentence):
If 7-day rolling revenue (usage) falls below scenario threshold X, enact pre-defined budget switch A and freeze non-critical hiring tranche Y until metric recovers for 3 consecutive weeks.

Trigger matrix (use as canonical):
CSV representation (TriggerName,Metric,Threshold,ImmediateAction,SecondaryAction,Owner,ETA-implement)
pricing-pressure-moderate,7-day-usage-drop,-12%,move 15% of feature marketing budget -> capacity buffer,defer 2 midsenior product hires,Finance Lead (Marcus),48-72h
pricing-pressure-severe,7-day-usage-drop,-20%,pause open requisitions in non-customer-facing roles,shift 25% of beta budget to credits for churned accounts,Head of Talent (Bianca),24-48h
high-latency-cost-leak,token-cost-per-hour,>+$0.12/hr above baseline,enable auto-routing to cheaper quantized variants for non-SLA routes,spin up temporary spot GPU reserve cap,Infra PM (Samir),6-12h
feature-sla-critical,customer-customer-uptake,>5 customers reporting regression,protect dedicated capacity budget (do not reflow),escalate to CTO and allocate emergency fund,Customer Success Lead (Aisha),immediate

Quick budget reflow table (editable weekly):
Bucket,CurrentMonthly,ReflowStepsIfModerate,ReflowStepsIfSevere
feature-marketing,120000,move 15% -> capacity-buffer,move 30% -> credits & customer-retention
pilot-credits,40000,freeze new pilots except strategic<->sales-path,reduce to 10k and re-prioritize enterprise pilots only
platform-rd,540000,freeze 1 non-critical hire,freeze 3 non-critical hires and defer 2 planned infra projects
ops-contractors,80000,convert 20% -> temp-hire pipeline,shrink to 40% and negotiate hourly discounts

Hiring tranche definitions (used by Talent to gate offers / reqs):
- Tranche A (critical): SLA, customer-facing eng, security/compliance. Not pausable.
- Tranche B (important): product feature leads, infra core modules. Pausable if severe trigger fires.
- Tranche C (nice-to-have): exploratory ML/infra proof-of-concepts, research internships. Freeze immediately under moderate/severe.

Sensitivity analysis (short notes + cliff numbers):
We ran three micro-scenarios focusing on pricing elasticity and the headcount-lag effect:
- Conservative scenario (-10% usage): sliding window reflow yields ~7% monthly spend savings with minimal hiring impact (delay Tranche C hires). Net margin delta +1.3 ppts.
- Baseline scenario (-18% usage): reflow + hiring freeze for Tranche B/C yields ~18% monthly cash preservation; runway extension ~4.6 weeks. Product delivery delays estimated at 6–10 weeks.
- Severe scenario (-25% usage): must implement severe actions: freeze B and C offers, move pilot credits to retention; cash preservation up to 30% of discretionary spend; runway extension ~9–10 weeks but with feature backlog growth and increased churn risk.
Key elasticities used: -0.42 take-rate elasticity at price change horizon (30-day lag), internal conversion loss of 2.8% per 1% effective price increase in lower-tier accounts.

Microcalc examples (for quick checks):
1) If monthly paid usage = $1.2M and shock = -18%: delta = -$216k. If reflow saves 18% of discretionary spend ($300k discretionary) = $54k offset -> residual -$162k. Weekly gate: if residual > -$150k for 2 weeks then resume 1 Tranche B req.
2) Token-cost mitigation: enabling routing + quantization expected to reduce marginal cost from $0.86 -> $0.76 per 1k tokens at 60% adoption. At 15M tokens/day this yields ~ $1.5k/day savings once adoption hits target.

Operational playbook (actionable steps):
- Week 0 (decision): finance issues a green/yellow/red signal to leads with the trigger firing reason.
- 0–72h: implement immediate budget moves (finance transfers chart-coded lines), Talent pauses or continues pipeline according to tranche.
- Weekly cadence: product/infra owners submit recovery readout (quant metrics + customer notes).
- 3-week rule: if metric recovers (usage within 5% of pre-shock) for 3 consecutive weekly snapshots, slowly unwind reflow (15% increments).
- Escalation: if severe triggers persist beyond 6 weeks, exec review for temporary hiring swaps and customer credit program reprioritization.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal (to execs): "Signal: RED — 7d usage -22%. Enacted: pause B/C, move 25% pilot budget to retention. Action owners: Marcus/Bianca. Ops: immediate."
- Customer-facing (CS templated): "We’re temporarily adjusting pilot credit availability while we stabilize pricing & capacity. Your pilot remains prioritized; assigned AE will reach out with an extension offer."

Open questions / items to model next sprint:
- More granular elasticity by cohort (enterprise vs small-mid). Confluence ticket linked above.
- Model combined effect of price + CTAs (credits) on net churn over 90 days.
- Validate infra cost telemetry for quantization candidate routes (required by Infra by 2026-05-10).

Owners and immediate tasks (this doc is the single source of truth for short-cycle actions):
- Finance lead (Marcus Liu): prepare transfer journal and weekly summary; implement CSV-coded transfers. (ETA 48h)
- Talent (Bianca Gomez): freeze/safeguard offers per tranche; maintain candidate pipeline for Tranche A. (ETA 24h)
- Infra PM (Samir Rao): enable routing flags + telemetry gating to measure marginal cost improvement. (ETA 72h)
- Author (Aisha Patel): run weekly reconciliation and circulate to Execs on Fridays.

Appendix (scratch calculations and raw numbers):
- Discretionary buckets: feature-marketing 120k/mo, pilot-credits 40k/mo, conference/travel 25k/mo, learning budget 18k/mo.
- Headcount pipeline snapshot (May 2026): 6 open reqs (2 A, 2 B, 2 C). Offers in flight: 1 B, 1 C.
- Quick note: avoid permanent headcount cuts as first-order lever; prefer temporary hiring pauses + contractor negotiation.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lightweight; convert to spreadsheet if we start running weekly reflows.
- Pull raw usage by cohort (billing) and push to /cost-tools weekly to validate the elasticity assumptions.
- Confirm with product which two infra projects are deferrable if severe scenario triggers.

End of worksheet.

(Author contact: aisha.patel@redwood.ai | Slack: @aisha — leave comments inline in this doc; keep weekly snapshots under the same filename with date prefix.)
